ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black) surface with approximately 15-20% high-intensity (white) pixel coverage consisting of small, discrete clusters and points.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous dark-intensity base layer across both lobes, populated by an irregular, high-frequency distribution of white punctate clusters (1-4 pixel diameter) concentrated primarily on the lower half and medial sections of the lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Central V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees and a depth ratio of 0.15 relative to the horizontal fluke span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency serrated boundary with jagged pixel peaks (3-15 pixel amplitude) and valleys along the entire trailing edge; serrations are more pronounced and irregular on the right lobe (viewer perspective).
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edge exhibits a consistent convex curvature from the median notch to the lateral tips, with the right lobe showing a more irregular, broken curve due to edge anomalies.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Extensive spatial detection of roughly circular, high-contrast white pixel clusters (rosettes) distributed semi-randomly across both the left and right ventral surfaces.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, non-parallel white linear pixel disruptions (scratches) visible on the right lobe, oriented diagonally toward the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A significant, deep semi-circular indentation or missing tissue segment on the trailing edge of the right lobe, approximately 60% of the distance from the notch to the tip.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique high-density stippled white pigmentation pattern across the dark base, creating a salt-and-pepper visual texture throughout the visible ventral surface.
